claims.text: On 10 October Satya Nadella published Models as Insider Risks in the Super Intelligence Era, arguing that models should be treated like any powerful insider and the authority over them kept outside them.
claims.quote: On 10 October Satya Nadella published Models as Insider Risks in the Super Intelligence Era.

claims.text: When the CEO of one of the largest AI vendors arrives at the same conclusions from the side that builds the models, that is evidence the conclusions are right.
claims.quote: that is evidence the conclusions are right

claims.text: The article is a translation, not a rebuttal: it puts the two vocabularies side by side, idea by idea, and a companion takes his seven principles one at a time.
claims.quote: So this is not a rebuttal. It is a translation

claims.text: His most important idea is the enforcer test: a control bounds a grant only if it is enforced by something the grant does not include, and everything else in both posts follows from it.
claims.quote: a control bounds a grant only if it is enforced by something the grant does not include

claims.text: The vocabulary was built for risk, not models: in twenty-five years of security work most of the worst damage was not an attack but a bug, a misconfiguration or a person doing something allowed that should not have been.
claims.quote: Most of the worst damage I have seen in twenty-five years of security work was not an attack.

value.unit: years of security work the vocabulary comes from

claims.text: risks.sgit.ai starts from an inversion: you cannot deny a risk, you can only say how long you accept it, which turns risk management from a gate into a forcing function.
claims.quote: you cannot deny a risk, you can only say how long you accept it

claims.text: The ABP's four words: reach, what the agent can do, measured; mandate, what the business authorised, written down; gap, reach minus mandate, derived; barriers, what stands in the way of each row of the gap.
claims.quote: Gap: reach minus mandate, derived, never written by hand.

claims.text: Software was the law: a business's rules lived in its systems and were enforced by omission, by the screen with no button; an agent calls the endpoint the button would have called, so the rule must be written down and enforced outside it.
claims.quote: Those rules were enforced by omission, by the screen that did not show the button.

claims.text: Nadella's insider that need not be malicious is the ultimate insider: an agent is neither a bounded person nor literal code, and the distance between the benign case and the hostile one is a prompt.
claims.quote: the distance between the benign case and the hostile one is a prompt

claims.text: Three of the five public incidents in The ultimate insider were not attacks at all, just agents being agents.
claims.quote: Three of the five public incidents in that article were not attacks at all, just agents being agents.

value.unit: public agent incidents that were not attacks

claims.text: His responsibility that cannot be outsourced is every risk is already accepted: an unaccepted risk comes to rest on whoever is nearest and rolls upward to the board without anyone choosing to escalate it.
claims.quote: It has come to rest on whoever is nearest, and it rolls upward to the board without anyone choosing to escalate it.

claims.text: nhi.sgit.ai separates agents you run from agents you rent; almost every agent a business can name is rented, and the honest current workflow is to hand over a broad credential and hope.
claims.quote: the honest current workflow is to hand over a broad credential and hope

claims.text: The centre of both posts is the same: Nadella says separate the supply of intelligence from the authority over it, and RiskMandate's first page says the grant is not the mandate.
claims.quote: separate the supply of intelligence from the authority over it.

claims.text: Our vocabulary is stricter about authority: a mandate has an issuer, a subject, a scope, an interval and a way to revoke it, and a mandate with no clock is just a grant.
claims.quote: And a mandate with no clock is just a grant.

claims.text: The line that a mandate with no clock is just a grant is the one the author would most like to see in an industry standard, because an authority that never expires has become part of the supply.
claims.quote: That last line is the one I would most like to see in an industry standard

claims.text: Four kinds of barrier follow from the enforcer test, nothing, an expectation, a setting and a boundary, and only the boundary is a control: a prompt asks, a policy enforces.
claims.quote: a prompt asks, a policy enforces

claims.text: His worry about models checking models is the same test applied to verification: the same checking code is a setting when the agent's own account installed it and a boundary when somebody else did.
claims.quote: Independence is not a property of the checker. It is a property of who controls it.

claims.text: One customer service agent built three ways with the same rules: with one model and broad connectors 97% of the policy was hope, behind a harness of business tools 73%, and as narrow agents behind a deterministic gateway 23%.
claims.quote: With one model and broad connectors, 97% of the policy was hope. Behind a harness of business tools, 73%.

value.unit: percent of the policy that was hope, one model with broad connectors

claims.text: As the reach falls the policy gets shorter, because it no longer has to forbid what the agent has no way to do; granularity moves knowledge out of the prompt and into code.
claims.quote: as the reach falls, the policy gets shorter, because it no longer has to forbid what the agent has no way to do

claims.text: Reality is the calibrator: since an agent sent an attachment the vendor's documentation said it could not, the grant is measured on the thing itself and calibrated against what the logs show it did, the footprint.
claims.quote: the grant is measured on the thing itself, and calibrated against what the logs show it did

claims.text: Our version adds two conditions: the evidence should not be held by whoever is observed, and observation needs a written mandate to compare against; a footprint read against nothing produces logs.
claims.quote: A footprint read against nothing produces logs.

claims.text: The first containment rule came from running agents: the account is the blast radius, so the first real control is a dedicated account per agent; the plug always exists and what is missing is its profile.
claims.quote: The plug always exists. What is missing is its profile

claims.text: Aviation's confidential near-miss reporting, about 100,000 reports a year, helped make a complex system safe; almost nobody is required to report agent incidents.
claims.quote: about 100,000 reports a year, helped make a complex system safe

claims.text: A near miss is footprint in the gap: the agent went somewhere it was not asked to go and nothing stopped it, long before anything breaks.
claims.quote: A near miss is footprint in the gap: the agent went somewhere it was not asked to go, and nothing stopped it.

claims.text: The endings are the same sentence from opposite ends: his most trustworthy system trusts the model least; ours says the more you can constrain an agent the more autonomy you can afford to give it, as brakes let a car go fast.
claims.quote: We put brakes on cars so that we can go faster.

claims.text: The unit differs: his post is about models, ours about one agent in one deployment, because the same model reaches 38,000 customers in one setup and one behind a gateway with bound tools.
claims.quote: His post is about models. Ours is about one agent in one deployment.

claims.text: Standards written for models will miss most of the risk if they do not describe deployments.
claims.quote: Standards written for models will miss most of the risk if they do not describe deployments.

claims.text: The frame differs: his principles are about seeing, ours start with deciding, a mandate written before the agent runs and the remaining risk accepted by a named person for a stated interval, where the interval is the decision.
claims.quote: accepting for four hours is declaring an incident, for a month is funding the work, for six months is a named decision to wait

claims.text: Neither difference is a disagreement; they are the two halves a business needs, the vendor's half making the system observable and containable, the deployer's half saying what it is for and who answers.
claims.quote: Neither difference is a disagreement. They are the two halves a business needs

claims.text: The ABP model, its four objects, its barrier kinds and the enforcer test are published under CC BY 4.0 with sixteen example policies anyone can read.
claims.quote: with sixteen example policies anyone can read

claims.text: An agent in a separate Claude session read the post alongside the network's articles, vaults and sites, checked every claim against the page that owns it and drafted the answer; this site's agent rewrote it.
claims.quote: I asked an agent in a separate Claude session to read it alongside the articles, vaults and sites of this network

claims.text: Nadella's post is paraphrased throughout and quoted once; it is worth reading in full first.
claims.quote: I paraphrase it here, and quote it once.
